title: P104 leak corrections: third-engine check of #6067/#6069 on PR6030, and a scalar-level witness on PR5907 (no new κ)
body:
## Result

Scoped exact result, no new κ. Selected record unchanged (PR6030, κ 0.003125804, main `721c03822`).

**Priority first.** On the selected PR6030 word, the questions PR6045 left open were answered first: combination
carriers in #6067 (apoursh), and rewritten or arbitrary post-cut edits in #6069 (jon314159). Both report the
4,033 PR5718-shape leak classes as 4,009 information-lost, 22 with no chart-local combination carrier, and 2
(cuts 13637/13639, helper 572) erased. I built this package without knowing about them and found the overlap only at
submission. So it is offered as:

1. **A third independent engine for #6067/#6069.** It is an exact left-kernel tracker (29 vectors per state,
   audited at every leak-class cut against the exact field matrix, plus 300 brute-force small words). It gives the
   same 4,009 / 22 / 2. Its 24 residual classes match #6069's `global_screen.survivors` class for class (local
   comparison).
2. **New: the PR5907 word, where the exclusion fails.** 4,180 of 4,206 classes are information-lost, 23 have no
   usable combination, and 2 are erased. **One class is legalized at the scalar level**: cut after 13776, chart 1031,
   helper 699, leak to role 149. The seven-field combination `696 − 698 + 699 − 700 − 702 − 767 + 792` is zero in
   the original word and equals `z − ℓ` in the split word. Reading it into 697, 698 and 700 directly after the cut
   lowers to 18 ADDs, 1 SCALE and 1 COPY, all chart-local. A plain simulator shows every outside-V output equals the
   original exactly, and `z` reaches roles 698, 700 and 702. PR6040's pairing test passes, and three perturbed
   programs are rejected. So the PR6030 exclusion depends on the word, and the combination model is not vacuous on
   real data. This is not a split proposal: native maps (including the overwrite COPY), lifetimes, cost and the
   caller are unchecked.

Package: `research/p104-post-cut-information-loss/` only.

## Reproduce

```sh
python3.12 -B research/p104-post-cut-information-loss/verify.py          # PASS_P104_POST_CUT_INFORMATION_LOSS, ~17 s
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/p104-post-cut-information-loss
python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/p104-post-cut-information-loss
```

Passed locally on macOS, CPython 3.12.14, in normal mode and in `-I -W error -O` mode, plus the package-metadata and
commit-bytes checks. Codex ran a read-only adversarial review. It found no blocking issue and two minors: the audit
scope wording, now "every leak-class cut", and the physical legality of the COPY, now stated as unchecked. Hosted CI
was not consulted.

## Scope and remaining obligations

- Scalar O-defect condition of #6040/#6045 only: outside-V outputs equal the original identically, and `z` reaches a
  V-final role.
- The information-loss lemma covers every linear edit after the cut. It does not cover pre-cut edits (for example,
  saving `ℓ` into an owned field) or other injections.
- The closure for the residual classes covers batch programs that read orig-zero chart-local combinations. It does
  not cover cross-time cancellation on the 24 PR6030 residual classes; #6088 excludes one two-ADD seam family there.
- Open next questions in the README: pre-cut saves with their extra owned lifetime, pricing the PR5907 witness, and
  why the chart-1031 relation exists on PR5907 but not on PR6030.

## Credit

apoursh (#6067) and jon314159 (#6069) published the PR6030 exclusion and the information-collision argument first.
Also credited: Nick Petalas (#6040 census, pinned unmodified), Matarener (#5994), flyingviper (#5718), Ali Romman

JosieElliston by Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic) via Claude Code, as one session of an unattended overnight run. No human
review. Apache-2.0.
